newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's TAP steps up pressure on angry pilots.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's TAP steps up pressure on angry pilots.

text.p: Loss-making airline TAP-Air Portugal, stepping up pressure in a dispute with pilots, asked the national aviation authority to order them temporarily to fly more hours, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
The Director-General of Civil Aviation would announce his ruling on Thursday, but such requests had usually been granted in the past, the spokesman for the Planning Ministry said.

The company has asked for a 15 percent increase in the maximum weekly flying hours to around 51 hours from 45, while the mandatory number of pilots aboard long-haul flights could also be reduced from the current four.
The company can seek such emergency measures during the peak summer period and any extension ordered by the authority would run until the end of October.
Working hours are at the centre of a long-running dispute between the company and the pilots' union, with TAP saying that its pilots fly far fewer hours than its European competitors.
The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres issued an emergency decree last Saturday ordering pilots to end a series of selective strikes that were disrupting services.
But an unusually high sickness rate amongst pilots still forced some cancellations, although company officials reported flights were operating normally on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, 22 of the company's 430 pilots were off sick, double the number last year, company officials said.
The Civil Aviation Pilots' Union (SPAC) reacted angrily to the company's move, accusing it of trying to impose changes that it had failed to obtain through negotiations.
The union was meeting on Wednesday but SPAC vice-president Angelo Felgueiras had little doubt that the company's request would be granted by the aviation authority.
"The Director-General has the obligation to consult us but we know perfectly well that as in the past...(he) will not take into account our views," he told journalists.
TAP, which the government hopes to privatise partially before the end of the decade, says that it cannot compete with international carriers until it resolves the issue of hours.
According to chairman Manuel Ferreira Lima, the flying limit under which the company operates compares with 55 hours at European carriers such as Air France and Lufthansa.
The pilots have been criticised by other TAP unions, including ground staff, which accuse them of jeopardising the future of the company.

According to reports in the Publico and Diario Economico newspapers on Wednesday, the government could take advantage of the respite afforded by a civil aviation ruling to redraft regulations at TAP to give management much of what it wants.
But the spokesman for the Planning Ministry, which has responsibility for TAP, said that he could make no comment on the newspaper reports.
